Issued at 251 AM CST Wed Nov 25 2026

Main forecast challenge with this forecast package is fine tuning 
snowfall totals and any potential impacts for tonight into 
Thanksgiving morning. Confidence is high that precipitation will 
begin as snow late tonight across the eastern CWA as the band of 
snow will move from east to west into the forecast area. Snow is 
then expected to fall for most of the event tonight into 
Thanksgiving morning before potentially mixing with rain as the 
precipitation exits Thanksgiving afternoon. So, although confidence 
is high in p-type and a extended duration of snow what is less 
confident is potential accumulation amounts and the level of impact. 
This is due to the surface temperatures hovering right around 
freezing for the duration of the event, snowfall rates being light 
throughout the event, as well as warm ground temperatures. That 
being said 1-3 inches of snow is forecast for areas along east of 
the Highway 65 corridor where some travel impacts are expected and 
as such a winter weather advisory has been issued from 10PM tonight 
through noon tomorrow. Further west, a dusting to less than an inch 
is forecast from Highway 65 back to the west to the Missouri/Kansas 
state line here little to no impacts are expected. 

In the lead up to our first winter event, the closed mid-level low 
that will be our weather maker will move directly over the forecast 
area providing for mostly cloudy skies. At the surface a weak 
surface ridge of high pressure will reside over the western CWA. 
Mostly cloudy conditions and weak mixing will hold highs in the 
upper 30s to mid 40s. Tonight this feature moves southwest of the 
CWA as Gulf moisture begin to to lift north across the Mississippi 
River Valley out ahead of the system. Tonight, a 700mb vort max 
wraps around the north side of the closed low bringing precipitation 
into the area from the east. Model soundings and temperature 
profiles indicate precipitation will arrive as snow. The 700mb vort 
max and snow will continue to retrograde back to the west and 
continue to spread light snow over the area from east to west. As 
previously mentioned surface temperatures will remain near freezing 
overnight into Thanksgiving morning and this coupled with light 
snowfall rates and warm ground temperatures may temper snow fall 
totals despite the fact that snow is expected from late tonight 
through tomorrow morning Totals of 1 to 3 inches are forecast are 
areas east of Highway 65 with totals less than an inch further west. 
Late tomorrow morning/early afternoon the 700mb vort max shift south 
and east of the area as the mid-level low shifts east into the Ohio 
River Valley bring precipitation to an end. Weak CAA behind this 
system on Thanksgiving Day will hold highs in the upper 30s to mid 
40s. 

A brief warming trend is anticipated Friday and Saturday. Friday, 
quasi-zonal flow aloft with modest WAA getting underway at the 
surface will aid in highs rising into the mid 40s to mid 50s. Friday 
night, a upper level shortwave rough will dig from the northern 
Plains into the Upper Midwest forcing a weak cold front through the 
area. Downsloping westerly flow behind the front on Saturday will 
help highs rise into the 50s to near 60. Sunday, models are 
consistent bring another upper level trough through the region. The 
EC is slower and deeper with this trough than its more progressive 
GFS counterpart. The EC solution brings greater chances for 
precipitation whereas the faster GFS provides weak lift and less of 
a moisture return. The current NBM current produces a 40-60% chance 
for rain Sunday although we may see probabilities lower if the GFS 
solution verifies. Either way, Sunday is still anticipated to be 
mild by late November standards with highs in the mid 40s to mid 
50s. Quasi-zonal flow aloft returns to the region on Monday with 
late day WAA aiding in highs rising into the upper 40s to mid 50s. 
Models push another upper level shortwave through the area on 
Tuesday the EC is dry with this feature whereas the GFS produces 
light showers. Current NBM probabilities keep conditions dry on 
Tuesday with mild conditions prevailing with forecast highs in the 
50s to near 60.
